items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to continuing the New York
State Smart Scholars Early College High School Program and the New York State
Pathways in Technology Early College High School Program in this state
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9060

SPONSOR: MARCELLINO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to continuing the New
York State Smart Scholars Early College High School Program and the New
York State Pathways in Technology Early College High School Program in
this state

 
PURPOSE:

To preserve and continue the New York State Smart Scholars early college
high school (NYS Smart Scholars ECHS) program and the New York State
pathways in technology early college high school (NYS P-TECH) program in
this State, which provides various students, including those tradi-
tionally underrepresented in post-secondary education, with the opportu-
nity to access college-level courses and college degree credits at the
high school level with the combined support of high school and college
staff and resources, .and for the NYS P-TECH programs, career training
and employment in a highly skilled job upon completion of the program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill adds a new Education Law § 6457 to establish grant
awards for NYS Smart Scholars ECHS programs. Subject to an appropri-
ation, the bill requires the Commissioner to allocate funds for NYS
Smart Scholars ECHS programs approved by the Commissioner in accordance
with the Commissioner's regulations and a request for proposals process.
The bill requires the Commissioner to prioritize partnerships that
demonstrate the willingness and capacity to serve students who have been
identified as economically disadvantaged and/or academically at-risk for
not successfully completing high school or not enrolling in or succeed-
ing in college.

This section of the bill defines an eligible applicant as a New York
State school district with a NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program with a
partnership with a not-for-profit higher education institution(s) to
offer college-level courses leading to the granting of at least 24
college credits and up to a post-secondary degree or diploma, or a not-
for-profit higher education institution registered with the Department
which partners with a New York State school district to offer a NYS
Smart Scholars ECHS program. It further defines an eligible student as a
student who is (i) a resident of the school district, or a resident of a
component district of a consortium applicant, in which the NYS Smart
Scholars ECHS program is located and is enrolled in such district; and
(ii) is registered to attend such high school for the academic years for
which the grant award is being sought.

Previously approved NYS Smart Scholars ECHS programs that were funded
under a prior request for proposals process, whose contracts have been
continuously renewed by the Department in accordance with all applicable
laws since the effective date of the new section shall be eligible for
continued funding without having to reapply for funding through a
competitive process unless they are seeking to offer a new NYS Smart
Scholars ECHS program; provided, however, that such previously approved
program shall be required to meet certain benchmarks and program
requirements as prescribed by the Department in order to demonstrate
that it continues to be a successful NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program and
if the program fails to meet certain benchmarks and program require-
ments, it may be subject to certain corrective action as described in
regulations of the Commissioner which may include but not be limited to
establishing timelines to meet program standards, a limitation on
enrollment, termination of the contract and/or closure of the program
and/or requiring a teach-out agreement with an approved NYS Smart Schol-
ars ECHS program to describe how students will be transferred to such
program upon closure.

This section also requires that monies made available under this section
can only be spent for the following purposes: to provide additional
staffing for the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program, including a program
director and college liaison; student recruitment activities; to provide
professional development to promote the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program,
including cross-curriculum development between secondary and post-secon-
dary education partners to ensure curriculum alignment that prepares
students to succeed in college level courses while in high school; work-
shops and planning meetings between partners, including counselors,
parents, and college faculty, to support program sustainability and
build awareness in the regions on the benefits of having such programs;
academic and social support services to promote college readiness and a
college-going culture; transportation for students to take courses and
participate in activities at the NYS Smart Scholars ECHS site and at the
campus of the higher education partner; and tuition, books and fees;
provided however that tuition reimbursement shall only be allowable for
non-remedial, credit-bearing college courses.

It further provides that no funds awarded under this section shall be
made available to support the regular academic program of any school
district or institution participating in this program.

Section 2 of the bill adds a new Education Law § 6458 to establish grant
awards for NYS P-TECH programs. Subject to an appropriation, the bill
requires the Commissioner to allocate funds for new P-TECH programs
approved by the Commissioner in accordance with the Commissioner's regu-
lations. This section defines eligible applicant as a New York State
school district or board of cooperative educational services, which must
serve as the fiscal agent. An eligible district may work in cooperation
with other school districts, a board of cooperative educational
services, or any combination of these entities with a partnership that
includes: (i) one or more New York State nonprofit higher education
institutions registered by the Department provided that at least one
institution offers an associate's degree linked to the goals of the
approved NYS P-TECH program, and which awards the degree at no cost to
the student/family; and (ii) a regional New York State employer and/or
industry/entity/association that requires highly skilled employees which
will utilize the knowledge and skills obtained from the secondary and
postsecondary programs proposed under the application and agrees to
place students who successfully complete the program with the opportu-
nity to be first in line for a job.

Previously approved NYS P-TECH programs that were funded under a prior
request for proposals process and whose contracts have been continuously
renewed by the Department in accordance with all applicable laws since
the effective date of the new section shall be eligible for continued
funding under this section without having to reapply for funding through
a competitive process unless they are seeking to offer a new NYS P-TECH
program; provided, however, that such previously approved program shall
be required to meet certain benchmarks and program requirements as
prescribed by the Department in order to demonstrate that it continues
to be a successful NYS P-TECH program and if the program fails to meet
certain benchmarks and program requirements, it may be subject to
certain corrective action as described in regulations of the Commission-
er which may include but not be limited to establishing timelines to
meet program standards, a limitation on enrollment, termination of the
contract and/or closure of the program and/or requiring a teach-out
agreement with an approved NYS P-TECH program to describe how students
will be transferred to such program upon closure.

Monies made available under this section can only be spent for the
following purposes: to provide additional staffing for the NYS P-TECH
program, including but not limited to a program director and a college
liaison; existing evidence-based and/or standards-based curriculum that
focuses on a career in science, technology, engineering or math- related
career area within a NYS P-TECH program; recruitment activities for
eligible students; to provide professional development to promote the
P-TECH program, including cross-curriculum development between partners
and to ensure curriculum alignment that prepares students to succeed in
college level courses while in high school and during career training;
up to ten percent of funds awarded under this section may be used for
eligible applicants to purchase equipment needed to upgrade existing
programs or new equipment to start a program; provided that an eligible
applicant may seek permission from the Commissioner for a waiver of the
ten percent cap, and such request must include a justification for why
equipment in excess of the cap is necessary to accomplish the goals of
the NYS P-TECH program; workshops and planning meetings between part-
ners, including counselors, parents, and college faculty, and business
leaders to support program sustainability and build awareness in the
regions of the benefits of having such programs; postsecondary curric-
ulum development that facilitates alignment and articulation with
secondary programs leading to college degrees and/or other industry
recognized credentials that meet the needs of employers; service
contracts between members of the partnership; transportation for eligi-
ble students to take courses and participate in activities at the NYS
P-TECH site, at partner employers' locations, and at the campus of the
higher education partner, and tuition, books and fees; provided that
tuition reimbursement will only be allowable for non-remedial, credit-
bearing college courses.

It further provides that no funds awarded under this section shall be
made available to support the regular academic program of any school
district or institution participating in this program.

Section 3 of the bill is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill is necessary to preserve and continue the NYS Smart Scholars
ECHS program and the New York State P-TECH program in the State which
provide various students, including those traditionally underrepresented
in post-secondary education, with the opportunity to access college-lev-
el courses and college degree credits at the high school level with the
combined support of high school and college staff and resources, and for

P-TECH programs, career training and employment in a highly skilled job
upon completion of the program.
The NYS Smart Scholars ECHS program not only increases student's access
to higher education, but also reduces potential costs for students in
completing college degrees by allowing them to either complete a degree
upon graduation from high school or to apply their earned college cred-
its towards an Associate's or Baccalaureate's degree. This innovative
program provides incentives to high school students to proceed to
college and to earn a college degree by accelerating their overall
completion of a degree. It also better prepares them for college-level
coursework, which increases their academic performance. Ultimately, this
Program increases graduation rates both at the high school and college
levels, especially for academically at-risk students.

The NYS P-TECH program, through a public-private partnership, prepares
thousands of New York students for high-skill jobs of the future in
technology, manufacturing, healthcare and finance The NYS P-TECH program
provides students with a rigorous, relevant and cost-free high school
and college education and a workplace learning environment with ongoing
mentoring by professionals in the chosen career sector to better prepare
these students for successful careers. Students also receive a commit-
ment from the participating employer to have the opportunity to be first
in line for consideration for a job following completion of the program.
Ultimately, this Program increases graduation rates both at the high
school and college levels and provides essential career training for
academically at-risk, disadvantaged students, which at the completion of
the Program leads these students to a skilled job.

The accelerated completion of a student's college degree at the high
school level will result in a student requiring less financial assist-
ance (including tuition assistance or TAP funds) to complete their
degree at the post-secondary level. These programs will ultimately
result in significant cost-savings to both the State and to families and
therefore, are a great investment of State funds.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

SED Proposal No. 14 for 2016 was introduced as S.  7496 (Marcelli-
no)/A.10024 (Nolan) and was referred to the Education Committees in the
Senate and Assembly. The bill moved to third reading in the Senate. No
further action was taken in the Assembly.

SED Proposal No. 1 of 2013 was introduced as S.4008-A (Flanagan) in 2013
and passed the Senate in 2013 and 2014.

SED Proposal No. 7 was introduced as S.5647 (Flanagan) in 2011 and
A.9312 (Nolan) in 2012 and was referred to the respective education
committees. The bill passed the Senate in 2011 and 2012. No further
action was taken in the Assembly.

New bill, extends Chapter 35 of 2015.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill shall take effect in 30 days.
